q-33037.name: Question 1
q-33037.problem:
Find an equation of the plane that passes through the point $Q(2,-3,5)$ and is perpendicular to the line that goes through the points 
$A(3,2,-8)$ and $B(1,2,-5).$
q-33037.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $Q$ is $q=⟨2,-3,5⟩.$

Since the line  passes through the points $A(3,2,-8)$ and $B(1,2,-5)$, we can find a vector that is parallel to the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =⟨1,2,-5⟩-⟨3,2,-8⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,0,3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

So, a normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨-2,0,3⟩.$

Therefore, the equation of the plane is given by 

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-q)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-q\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =q\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-2,0,3⟩ & =⟨2,-3,5⟩\cdot ⟨-2,0,3⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-2,0,3⟩ & =11.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Find an equation of the plane that passes through the point Q(2,−3,5) and is perpendicular to the line that goes through the points A(3,2,−8) and B(1,2,−5).

a
r⋅⟨2,−3,5⟩=−11
b
r⋅⟨−2,0,3⟩=⟨2,−3,5⟩
c
r⋅⟨−2,0,3⟩=11
d
r⋅⟨2,−3,5⟩=⟨−2,0,3⟩
e
r⋅⟨2,−3,5⟩=11
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we note that the position vector of Q is q=⟨2,−3,5⟩.

Since the line passes through the points A(3,2,−8) and B(1,2,−5), we can find a vector that is parallel to the line:

AB→=⟨1,2,−5⟩−⟨3,2,−8⟩=⟨−2,0,3⟩

So, a normal vector to the plane is n=⟨−2,0,3⟩.

Therefore, the equation of the plane is given by

(r−q)⋅n=0r⋅n−q⋅n=0r⋅n=q⋅nr⋅⟨−2,0,3⟩=⟨2,−3,5⟩⋅⟨−2,0,3⟩r⋅⟨−2,0,3⟩=11.

q-70895.name: Question 2
q-70895.problem:
Find an equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(3,-5,-2)$ and is perpendicular to the line 

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=2-3t \\ y=3+4t \\ z=4-t.\end{aligned}
$$
q-70895.worked_solution:
Note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨3,-5,-2⟩.$ Converting the parametric equations of the line to vector form, we get

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=2-3t \\ y=3+4t \\ z=4-t\end{aligned}\,⟹\,⟨x,y,z⟩=⟨2,3,4⟩+t\text{ }{{⟨-3,4,-1⟩}_{⏟}}_{v}.
$$

 

The direction vector of the line is $v=⟨-3,4,-1⟩,$ so a normal vector to the plane is 

$$
n=v=⟨-3,4,-1⟩.
$$

Therefore, the equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-p\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-3,4,-1⟩ & =⟨3,-5,-2⟩\cdot ⟨-3,4,-1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-3,4,-1⟩ & =-27.\end{aligned}
$$

q-70895.html:
Question 2
?

Find an equation of the plane that passes through the point P(3,−5,−2) and is perpendicular to the line {x=2−3ty=3+4tz=4−t.

a
r⋅⟨3,−5,−2⟩=⟨−3,4,−1⟩
b
r⋅⟨3,−5,−2⟩=−27
c
r⋅⟨−3,4,−1⟩=0
d
r⋅⟨−3,4,−1⟩=−27
e
r⋅⟨−3,4,−1⟩=⟨3,−5,−2⟩
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Note that the position vector of P is p=⟨3,−5,−2⟩. Converting the parametric equations of the line to vector form, we get {x=2−3ty=3+4tz=4−t⟹⟨x,y,z⟩=⟨2,3,4⟩+t ⟨−3,4,−1⟩⏟v.

The direction vector of the line is v=⟨−3,4,−1⟩, so a normal vector to the plane is n=v=⟨−3,4,−1⟩.

Therefore, the equation of the plane is given by

(r−p)⋅n=0r⋅n−p⋅n=0r⋅n=p⋅nr⋅⟨−3,4,−1⟩=⟨3,−5,−2⟩⋅⟨−3,4,−1⟩r⋅⟨−3,4,−1⟩=−27.

q-127910.name: Question 3
q-127910.problem: A nonzero vector $⟨a,\,0,\,c⟩$ is parallel to the plane $r\cdot ⟨-1,1,3⟩=\sqrt{7}.$ What is the value of $\frac{a}{c}?$
q-127910.worked_solution:
We need a vector $v=⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩$ that is parallel to the given plane. 

From the equation $r\cdot ⟨-1,1,3⟩=\sqrt{7}$ of the plane, we get the normal vector $n=⟨-1,1,3⟩.$ So, $v⊥n$ and we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot n & =0 \\ ⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩\cdot ⟨-1,1,3⟩ & =0 \\ -{t}_{1}+{t}_{2}+3{t}_{3} & =0 \\ {t}_{1} & ={t}_{2}+3{t}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we obtain 

$$
v=⟨{t}_{2}+3{t}_{3},\,{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩,
$$

where ${t}_{2},{t}_{3}\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

We are told that the second component of $v$ equals $0.$ So, we must set ${t}_{2}=0.$ 

Since $v$ is nonzero, we can pick any ${t}_{3}\ne 0.$ For example, setting ${t}_{3}=1$, we get

$$
v=⟨3,\,0,\,1⟩.
$$

Therefore, $\frac{a}{c}=3.$

q-127910.html:
Question 3
?

A nonzero vector ⟨a,0,c⟩ is parallel to the plane r⋅⟨−1,1,3⟩=7. What is the value of ac?

a
−1
b
1
c
−3
d
7
e
3
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We need a vector v=⟨t1,t2,t3⟩ that is parallel to the given plane.

From the equation r⋅⟨−1,1,3⟩=7 of the plane, we get the normal vector n=⟨−1,1,3⟩. So, v⊥n and we have the following:

v⋅n=0⟨t1,t2,t3⟩⋅⟨−1,1,3⟩=0−t1+t2+3t3=0t1=t2+3t3

Hence, we obtain

v=⟨t2+3t3,t2,t3⟩,

where t2,t3∈(−∞,∞).

We are told that the second component of v equals 0. So, we must set t2=0.

Since v is nonzero, we can pick any t3≠0. For example, setting t3=1, we get

v=⟨3,0,1⟩.

Therefore, ac=3.

q-127921.name: Question 4
q-127921.problem: A nonzero vector $⟨0,\,b,\,c⟩$ is parallel to the plane $r\cdot ⟨5,-1,3⟩=27.$ What is the value of $\frac{b}{c}?$
q-127921.worked_solution:
We need a vector $v=⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩$ that is parallel to the given plane. 

From the equation $r\cdot ⟨5,-1,3⟩=27$ of the plane, we get the normal vector $n=⟨5,-1,3⟩.$ So, $v⊥n$ and we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot n & =0 \\ ⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩\cdot ⟨5,-1,3⟩ & =0 \\ 5{t}_{1}-{t}_{2}+3{t}_{3} & =0 \\ {t}_{2} & =5{t}_{1}+3{t}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we obtain 

$$
v=⟨{t}_{1},\,5{t}_{1}+3{t}_{3},\,{t}_{3}⟩,
$$

where ${t}_{1},{t}_{3}\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

We are told that the first component of $v$ equals $0.$ So, we must set ${t}_{1}=0.$ 

Since $v$ is nonzero, we can pick any ${t}_{3}\ne 0.$ For example, setting ${t}_{3}=1$, we get

$$
v=⟨0,\,3,\,1⟩.
$$

Therefore, $\frac{b}{c}=3.$

q-127956.name: Question 5
q-127956.problem:
Find an equation of the plane that passes through the point $Q(4,-2,3)$ and is  perpendicular to the line 

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-1+2t \\ y=3-2t \\ z=5+t.\end{aligned}

$$

$$

q-127956.html:
Question 5
?

Find an equation of the plane that passes through the point Q(4,−2,3) and is perpendicular to the line {x=−1+2ty=3−2tz=5+t.

a
r⋅⟨2,−2,1⟩=15
b
r⋅⟨4,−2,1⟩=18
c
r⋅⟨−2,2,1⟩=12
d
r⋅⟨1,−2,4⟩=22
e
r⋅⟨1,−4,−2⟩=8
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Note that the position vector of Q is q=⟨4,−2,3⟩. Converting the parametric equations of the line to vector form, we get {x=−1+2ty=3−2tz=5+t⇒⟨x,y,z⟩=⟨−1,3,5⟩+t ⟨2,−2,1⟩⏟v.

The direction vector of the line is v=⟨2,−2,1⟩. So, a normal vector to the plane is n=v=⟨2,−2,1⟩.

Therefore, the equation of the plane is given by

(r−q)⋅n=0r⋅n−q⋅n=0r⋅n=q⋅nr⋅⟨2,−2,1⟩=⟨4,−2,3⟩⋅⟨2,−2,1⟩r⋅⟨2,−2,1⟩=15.
